comment: parapet v3.0.0-APACHE seccomp profile. Default: DENY ALL. Only syscalls required by Ollama + Python inference are whitelisted. This is evidence for upgrading Patent #5 from 5-Layer to 6-Layer Container Security.

syscalls.comment: ── Basic I/O ── Required by Python runtime, file descriptor operations, stdin/stdout/stderr. Every user-space process needs these fundamental operations.
── File Metadata ── Required for file existence checks, size queries, symlink resolution. Ollama reads GGUF model files, tokenizer configs, and Modelfiles.
── Directory Operations ── Required for scanning model directories, listing workspace files, the RAG index scans workspace trees.

── Memory Management ── CRITICAL. Ollama loads multi-GB GGUF models via mmap(). mprotect() sets executable pages for JIT-compiled kernels. mlock() pins model weights in GPU-accessible memory. brk() extends heap for Python objects.

── GPU / CUDA Communication ── CRITICAL. ioctl() is the primary syscall for NVIDIA GPU driver communication. CUDA kernels, VRAM allocation, and tensor operations all funnel through ioctl() on the GPU device node.

── Threading & Synchronization ── Ollama uses multi-threaded inference with pthreads. futex() is the kernel primitive for mutexes, condition variables, and thread synchronization. clone/clone3 create new threads. set_robust_list handles thread crash recovery.

── Network ── Localhost Only ── Communication between ollama-agent and ollama-web-ui containers, and between containers and host Ollama (localhost:11434). All communication stays within Docker bridge network. socket() with AF_INET/AF_UNIX only.
── Async I/O ── Required by Python asyncio (FastAPI/uvicorn), Ollama streaming responses, SSE event streams for the web UI, and concurrent request handling.

── Process Lifecycle ── exit/exit_group for clean shutdown. getpid/gettid for logging. rt_sigaction/rt_sigprocmask for signal handling (SIGTERM graceful shutdown, SIGCHLD reaping). tgkill for thread termination.
── Time ── clock_gettime() used by Python's time.monotonic(), CUDA timing, benchmark measurements. nanosleep() for polling loops and rate limiting.
── Scheduling & Affinity ── sched_getaffinity/setaffinity allow thread pinning for optimal GPU inference performance. sched_yield allows cooperative multitasking between inference threads.
── System Information ── uname() for OS detection in Python. sysinfo() for memory stats. getrusage() for profiling. prlimit64() for resource limit queries.
── Randomness & Security ── getrandom() used by Python secrets module for token generation (auth tokens, crypto keys). Also used by TLS libraries if HTTPS is enabled for web UI.

── Thread-Local Storage ── set_tid_address() and arch_prctl() are called by glibc during thread creation. Essential for any multi-threaded Linux process. prctl() used by Docker runtime for process naming.
── Extended Attributes ── Required by Docker overlay filesystem and some Python file operations on modern kernels.
── File Descriptor Control ── fcntl() for non-blocking I/O, FD_CLOEXEC, file locking. Required by Python's socket and file I/O.
── Resource Statistics ── getrusage() for performance monitoring. getrlimit() for checking system limits before loading large models.
── Timers ── timerfd_create/timerfd_settime used by Python asyncio event loop for timeouts. setitimer/getitimer for interval profiling.
── Event FD ── eventfd2() used by glibc for inter-thread signaling in the pthreads implementation. Essential for multi-threaded inference.

── Memory Mapping Control ── fallocate() reserves disk space for large model cache files. fadvise64() hints kernel about file access patterns for faster model loading. ftruncate() resizes files. sync/fsync flush model writes.
── Inotify ── File change monitoring used by Python auto-reload (uvicorn --reload) and workspace file watchers.
── Capability Operations ── capget/capset for capability bounding set queries. prctl(PR_CAP_AMBIENT) for ambient capability clearing.
── UTS Namespace ── sethostname used by Docker to set container hostname. Required during container initialization phase only; after that it's unused.
── Clipboard ── mremap and mlock2 are the modern versions of mremap/mlock. Included for glibc compatibility on newer kernel versions.
── process_madvise ── Memory advice for process-level page reclamation. Used by glibc malloc on modern kernels for heap optimization.
── pidfd operations ── Modern glibc uses pidfd_open/pidfd_getfd for child process management. Required by Python subprocess and Docker health checks.

── Filesystem Mutations ── Required for workspace directory creation (mkdir), file deletion (unlink), renaming, symlinks, and permission changes. The agent creates workspace subdirectories and manages session files. chmod 0o600 is called by crypto_vault on key files.

── User/Group Identity ── glibc calls getuid/geteuid/getgid/getegid/getgroups at process startup to initialize thread-local identity caches. Without these, Python crashes with 'failed to get user ID'. These are purely read-only identity queries -- no privilege changes.

── Process Forking ── fork/vfork/clone are required by Python's subprocess.run() for shell command execution. wait4/waitid reap child processes. Without fork, ANY shell command (even 'echo hello') crashes the agent.

── glibc Runtime Essentials ── membarrier() is used by glibc for thread synchronization on modern kernels. eventfd() is an alternative to eventfd2. close_range() efficiently closes fd ranges. umask() controls default file permissions. getdents() is the legacy directory reader.
── Signal Queue ── rt_sigqueueinfo/rt_tgsigqueueinfo allow sending signals with additional data. Used by glibc for thread cancellation and some pthreads operations on newer kernels.
── AIO ── Async I/O used by some database and storage libraries. Included for future-proofing -- not currently used by Ollama but may be needed for vector database operations.
── io_uring ── Modern Linux async I/O interface. Used by Python 3.12+ and some networking libraries for high-performance I/O. Included for future compatibility.

── Resource Limits ── setrlimit() and prlimit64() allow querying and setting resource limits. The agent queries limits before loading large models to check available memory. Only lower limits can be set (can never exceed Docker's limits).
── Timestamp Updates ── utimensat/futimesat update file timestamps. Used by Python's pathlib and shutil when writing files.
── Namespace Operations ── setns() allows joining an existing namespace. Used by Docker runtime during container initialization.

── seccomp Self-Reference ── seccomp() syscall is needed by child processes that inherit the seccomp filter. Without it, fork+exec fails because the child cannot query or modify its own seccomp state.
── Landlock ── Linux Landlock is a modern unprivileged access control mechanism. Programs that use Landlock to self-restrict (e.g., Python sandboxing) need these syscalls.

── Ownership (Non-privileged) ── chown/fchown/fchownat are included because some Python file operations call them for no-op ownership checks. With CAP_CHOWN dropped, these syscalls always fail with EPERM -- they're allowed at the seccomp layer but blocked at the capability layer. This is defense in depth.
